title: Who needs high-concentration protein formulations, and how fast is that growing?
question: Is there real, growing demand for the formulations orbit-grown protein crystals could serve (subcutaneous high-dose antibodies), and for the commodities our other candidates touch (lithium)?

headline.text: Since 2020 the FDA has licensed subcutaneous versions of 16 antibodies first licensed as IV infusions (Keytruda Qlex in Sep 2025), and registered SC antibody trials grew from 31 starting in 2005 to about 248 a year in 2021-2025.

compute.where: MIT Engaging (ClinicalTrials.gov download and parse); laptop (FDA, USGS, assembly)

method: Downloaded the full ClinicalTrials.gov registry as one bulk JSON zip on MIT Engaging and streamed all study files inside the zip with 6 worker processes (no extraction).

Kept interventional studies. An antibody intervention is one whose name or other names contain an INN monoclonal-antibody stem word (-mab), 'monoclonal antibody' or 'mAb'; a biologic is interventionType BIOLOGICAL or an antibody.

Route text is attributed to the antibody itself: its own name, other names and description, and text windows around its name in arm descriptions and titles, cut at the nearest mention of any other intervention so the route of co-administered chemotherapy or vaccines is not counted.

Primary route definition: full words (subcutaneous, intravenous) plus abbreviations in a dosing context (SC/IV after a dose unit or before injection/infusion/dose/every/q3w..., s.c., i.v., subQ) plus 'infusion' for IV (not subcutaneous infusion or infusion reactions). Sensitivity: full words only, and a crude trial-wide match.

Counted one study once per start year (startDateStruct); SC share = studies with an SC antibody route / studies with any stated SC or IV antibody route, with Wilson 95% intervals. 2026 is partial and includes planned start dates.
Hand-checked the classifier on a deterministic 2% hash sample of antibody studies (20 SC-positive, 20 IV-positive).

Counted antibody interventions co-formulated with a hyaluronidase or named by an SC brand/code (Faspro, Hybreza, Qvantig, Qlex, Zunovo, Phesgo, MK-3475A...) as a high-precision marker of IV-to-SC reformulation programmes.

From the FDA Purple Book (every licensed biologic), took antibody BLAs (INN -mab in the proper name), dated each by its first approval date and its route then; for originator products found each antibody's first IV and first SC licence and listed those that went IV first, SC later. Cross-checked first-approval dates against openFDA Drugs@FDA.
Joined USGS DS140 world lithium-content production (2000-2021) with MCS 2022, 2024 and 2026 world totals (2020-2025), latest edition winning.

findings: Across the full ClinicalTrials.gov registry (608,415 studies), 25,470 interventional studies test an INN '-mab' antibody.
Studies that give an antibody subcutaneously grew from 31 starting in 2005 to 248 a year on average in 2021-2025 (about 8.0x).
The SC share of route-stated antibody studies was 15% in 2005-2009, peaked at 34% in 2014, and was 21% in 2020-2025 (95% CI 20-22%).

Part of that dip is the IV checkpoint-inhibitor boom: PD-1/PD-L1/CTLA-4/LAG-3 antibodies went from 2% of antibody-level IV mentions in 2005 to 50% in 2020; excluding them the SC share is 30% in 2020 (vs 40% in 2014), so it still fell, but less. These IV checkpoint antibodies are the pool now being converted to SC (nivolumab, atezolizumab, pembrolizumab).
With full words only (no abbreviations) the shares are higher (26% in 2005-2009, 29% in 2020-2025) because IV is more often abbreviated; the rise-then-plateau shape is the same.

The FDA Purple Book lists 21 antibodies licensed IV first that later gained an SC product under a 351(a) (non-biosimilar) licence; 16 of those SC licences came in 2020 or later: daratumumab (Darzalex Faspro, 2020-05), pertuzumab (Phesgo, 2020-06), ofatumumab (Kesimpta, 2020-08), ravulizumab (Ultomiris, 2022-06), vedolizumab (Entyvio, 2023-09), infliximab (Zymfentra, 2023-10), spesolimab (Spevigo, 2024-03), atezolizumab (Tecentriq Hybreza, 2024-09), ocrelizumab (Ocrevus Zunovo, 2024-09), nivolumab (Opdivo Qvantig, 2024-12), lecanemab (Leqembi IQLIK, 2025-08), pembrolizumab (Keytruda Qlex, 2025-09), mosunetuzumab (Lunsumio Velo, 2025-12), amivantamab (Rybrevant Faspro, 2026-02), anifrolumab (Saphnelo, 2026-04), isatuximab (Sarclisa Escena, 2026-07).
New originator antibody licences that include an SC product at first approval: 3/20 in 1994-2004, 6/25 in 2005-2014, 25/52 in 2015-2019 and 31/86 in 2020-2026 (FDA Purple Book).
9 licensed antibody products are co-formulated with a hyaluronidase: today's main route to high-dose SC antibodies is enzyme-assisted injection, not crystalline suspensions.
ClinicalTrials.gov holds 143 studies (start 2005-2026) of antibodies co-formulated with a hyaluronidase or named by an SC brand/code, a direct count of IV-to-SC reformulation programmes.
World lithium mine production rose from 32,200 t (2015) to an estimated 290,000 t in 2025 (9.0x, USGS, lithium content, excluding the US).
Hand check of the route classifier: 18/20 SC calls and 19/20 IV calls were correct on a deterministic sample; 38.2% of sampled antibody studies state no route at all.
limitations: Registered trials are a proxy for formulation demand. They do not measure doses, patients, sales or willingness to pay, and they say nothing yet about demand for orbit-grown crystals specifically.

Route is inferred from free text with regular expressions. Precision is reported from a hand check, recall is lower: 30-40% of antibody studies state no route in the fields we read, and those are excluded from the share.

The '-mab' INN stem misses antibodies known only by code names (e.g. MK-3475 alone) and antibodies named under the 2021+ INN scheme (-tug, -bart, -mig, -ment); 'biologic' (interventionType BIOLOGICAL) also includes vaccines and cell therapies.

Start year is not approval year; 2026 is a partial year and includes planned (estimated) start dates. Registration practice changed over time (ICMJE 2005, FDAAA 2007, the 2017 Final Rule), so early-year counts are not strictly comparable.
One study counts once even if it has many arms; studies are not independent of each other (one sponsor runs many related trials of one molecule).

Purple Book counts are licences by route, not sales; route is read from the product listing, and our IV-to-SC list is restricted to originator (351(a)) products. Drugs@FDA covers only CDER BLAs and its route field is often just 'INJECTION', so it is used only as a date cross-check.

SC demand is being met today mainly by hyaluronidase co-formulation and high-concentration liquids. Crystalline suspensions (Merck's published pembrolizumab work) are one alternative; this analysis does not show they will win.
Lithium: production is a supply series, US consumption is withheld after 2021, the 2023 value is an MCS 2024 estimate, and 2024-2025 are USGS estimates. It does not show demand for MOF membranes.
No solid-state / barocaloric cooling demand series was added: we found no quick, real public market series and did not substitute one.
future_big_data: Link ClinicalTrials.gov interventions to RxNorm/UNII and to the FDA SPL label corpus (openFDA label bulk, ~1.8 GB zipped) to read the route and concentration (mg/mL) of every antibody product, instead of free-text regex.
Add the EU Clinical Trials Register / CTIS and WHO ICTRP to cover non-US registrations, and the AACT relational snapshot for a dated history of protocol changes (IV-to-SC amendments).
Use IQVIA-type or CMS Part B/Part D spending data to turn trial counts into dollars spent on IV infusion chair-time that SC conversion would remove.
Text-mine patents (USPTO/EPO full text) for 'crystalline suspension' antibody formulations to size the specific crystal-formulation pipeline.
For lithium, add USGS country-level production, IEA battery demand and direct-lithium-extraction project databases to size the separation-membrane market.

partners.name: Merck & Co. (MSD)
partners.why: Owns pembrolizumab, the project's published protein-crystal anchor, and has just moved it from IV to SC; a crystalline high-concentration suspension is a direct alternative formulation route.
partners.evidence: FDA Purple Book: Keytruda Qlex licensed 2025-09-19 (11.0 years after IV Keytruda); ClinicalTrials.gov: 12 Merck-sponsored hyaluronidase/SC-brand antibody studies, e.g. NCT03486873, NCT05017012, NCT05722015, NCT06041802. Merck's ISS pembrolizumab crystallization is a published result (Reichert et al., npj Microgravity 2019).

partners.name: Johnson & Johnson (Janssen)
partners.why: Runs IV-to-SC antibody reformulation programmes, i.e. is already paying to make high-dose SC antibody formulations.
partners.evidence: FDA Purple Book SC licences: daratumumab (Darzalex Faspro, 2020-05-01); amivantamab (Rybrevant Faspro, 2026-02-13). ClinicalTrials.gov: 4 hyaluronidase/SC-brand antibody studies with this lead sponsor.
